mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has declined for three consecutive weeks (-9.4 to -23.0). This momentum reflects an ongoing contraction in discretionary mobility that will persist absent a shock, pushing the next 4-week mean below the last 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC fell monotonically each of the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: Next 4-week mean RETAIL_REC exceeds last 4-week mean despite the prior 3-week monotonic decline, i.e. the trend reverses without any proxy signal change.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility rising above +12 points while TRANSIT sits below -60 indicates active stay-at-home policy enforcement. Once RESIDENTIAL crosses a +12 threshold concurrently with TRANSIT below -55, retail trips are further suppressed by legal/behavioral compliance over the next 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL > 12 AND TRANSIT < -55 simultaneously in the same week
evidence_refs: fact:t-1w RESIDENTIAL=13.7 TRANSIT=-61.9; t-0w RESIDENTIAL=12.3 TRANSIT=-61.6
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 2 weeks even though RESIDENTIAL remains above 12 and TRANSIT remains below -55.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous deep troughs in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES jointly indicate suppressed commuting capacity; their combined weakness compounds to reduce incidental retail visits (e.g., lunchtime or post-work shopping) beyond what either series predicts alone, lowering RETAIL_REC over the next 2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both deeply negative across all 4 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 2 weeks while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain jointly depressed below -50 and -30 respectively.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES rebounded sharply from -58.1 at t-2w to -33.0 at t-0w, a 25-point improvement suggesting early easing of workplace restrictions. If this reopening signal persists, RETAIL_REC should follow with a lagged recovery within 4 weeks as commuting-linked retail activity resumes.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES improves by more than 20 points over two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues to decline over the next 4 weeks despite WORKPLACES sustaining its recovery above -35.

mechanism_narrative: Volatile PARKS mobility (swinging from -19.3 to +12.0 to -11.3 to -15.9) indicates households substituting outdoor recreation for retail-linked recreation trips when parks access is favorable, temporarily depressing RETAIL_REC in weeks following a PARKS spike.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises more than 20 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall in the week immediately following a PARKS spike exceeding 20 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: The snapshot reflects Melbourne's cooler season, when reduced daylight and lower temperatures structurally depress outdoor and retail foot traffic independent of policy, reinforcing the downward RETAIL_REC trend over the next 4 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both RETAIL_REC and PARKS trend negative across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 4 weeks even though PARKS and RETAIL_REC both remain in negative territory, indicating season is not the binding constraint.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has collapsed from +9.9 to +1.1, showing essential-trip consolidation fatigue; once GROCERY_PHARM falls below +2, households have exhausted pantry-stocking behavior and further reduce all discretionary (retail) outings, driving RETAIL_REC lower over the next 2 weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined from 9.9 to 1.1 over the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stabilizes or rises over the next 2 weeks despite GROCERY_PHARM remaining below +2.

mechanism_narrative: A joint deterioration in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT alongside a rise in RESIDENTIAL signals compounding lockdown severity; when all three move adversely in the same week, the interacting suppression of mobility channels drives a sharper RETAIL_REC decline than any single series implies, persisting across the next 4 weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both decline week-on-week while RESIDENTIAL rises week-on-week
evidence_refs: fact:t-2w shows WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both falling while RESIDENTIAL rises to 10.9
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline further over the next 4 weeks even when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT fall together with RESIDENTIAL rising in the same week.
